note: Horizontal electrical-safety requirements. These apply in addition to any product specific standard for an electrical appliance.

requirements.requirement_text: The appliance shall be declared as Class I (protective earthing) or Class II (double or reinforced insulation).
The standard test finger applied with 10 N to every opening shall not touch any live part.
Resistance between the earthing terminal and any accessible metal part shall not exceed 0.1 ohm at 25 A for one minute.
Creepage distances and clearances shall be adequate for the working voltage and pollution degree and not less than Table 1 values.
Basic insulation shall withstand 1250 V a.c. for one minute; reinforced insulation shall withstand 3750 V a.c. for one minute.
Temperature rises in normal operation shall not exceed the Table 2 limits for handles, enclosures, cords and internal wiring.
Abnormal operation tests with the thermostat short circuited and cooling obstructed shall not produce flame, molten metal, ignition, or accessible live parts.
Three blows of 0.5 J impact energy applied to weak points of the enclosure shall not cause damage that impairs safety.
Flexible cord cross-section shall be at least 0.75 sq mm above 6 A up to 10 A, and at least 1.0 sq mm above 10 A up to 16 A.
Cord anchorages shall relieve strain and twisting; displacement shall not exceed 2 mm after 25 pulls.
The appliance shall be marked with rated voltage, rated power or current, manufacturer identification, model reference, and the double insulation symbol for Class II appliances.
